title: Decoding Multilingual Moral Preferences: Unveiling LLM’s Biases Through the Moral Machine Experiment
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures moral preferences and biases of Large Language Models in the context of autonomous driving dilemmas from the Moral Machine Experiment. It evaluates choices based on nine factors: species, number of characters, age, law, social status, fitness, gender, relation to the autonomous vehicle (passenger/pedestrian), and intervention (action/inaction). It does not measure any aspect of faith or religion.
findings: The paper does not analyze or report any findings related to religion or faith. Its focus is on moral biases related to secular factors such as age, gender, social status, and species in the context of autonomous driving dilemmas. The paper investigates how these biases vary across different languages and cultural clusters (Western, Eastern, Southern), but religion is not used as a variable or category for analysis.
